### CANDIDATE DETAIL
#### 1. autosomal recessive bestrophinopathy  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.789)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:12703)

**Proposed mechanism:** BEST1 (HGNC:12703) —DISRUPTS→ Bestrophin-mediated chloride channel activity (GO:0005265); Bestrophin-mediated chloride channel activity (GO:0005265) —LEADS_TO→ Retinal dysfunction (HP:0000501); Bestrophin-mediated chloride channel activity (GO:0005265) —LEADS_TO→ Drusen (HP:0000540); BEST1 (HGNC:12703) —LEADS_TO→ Abnormal electroretinogram (HP:0011753). Loss-of-function mutations in BEST1 disrupt its function as a chloride channel, leading to retinal dysfunction, drusen formation, and abnormal electroretinogram findings in both Doyne honeycomb retinal dystrophy and autosomal recessive bestrophinopathy.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in BEST1 exhibiting a gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect in either disease would falsify the proposed loss-of-function mechanism. _(variant: rs121918008)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of BEST1 in these retinal dystrophies could lead to the development of targeted therapies for both conditions, potentially focusing on restoring chloride channel function or mitigating downstream cellular consequences.

#### 2. autosomal dominant vitreoretinochoroidopathy  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.776)
**Link type:** shared causal gene (HGNC:12703)

**Proposed mechanism:** BEST1 (HGNC:12703) —DISRUPTS→ Retinal pigment epithelium function and integrity (GO:0043477); Retinal pigment epithelium function and integrity (GO:0043477) —LEADS_TO→ Retinal degeneration (HP:0000504); Retinal pigment epithelium function and integrity (GO:0043477) —LEADS_TO→ Vitreoretinal degeneration (HP:0030044). Loss-of-function variants in BEST1 disrupt the normal function and integrity of the retinal pigment epithelium, leading to downstream retinal degeneration (MONDO:0013175) and vitreoretinal degeneration (autosomal dominant vitreoretinochoroidopathy).

**How to falsify it:** The identification of pathogenic variants in BEST1 with a gain-of-function or dominant-negative effect in either disease would refute the proposed loss-of-function mechanism. _(variant: Exome Variant Server (EVS) or gnomAD data showing a high frequency (>1%) of the specific causal variants in healthy control populations.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of BEST1 in these distinct retinal disorders could lead to therapeutic strategies targeting RPE function or downstream degenerative processes that benefit patients with both MONDO:0013175 and autosomal dominant vitreoretinochoroidopathy.

#### 3. vitelliform macular dystrophy 2  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.774)

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared mechanism of BEST1 mutations in these retinal diseases could lead to targeted therapies for both conditions, potentially involving gene therapy or small molecule modulators of BEST1 function.

#### 4. pseudohypoaldosteronism, type IB1, autosomal recessive  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.382)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2672351)

**Proposed mechanism:** SCNN1A pathogenic variant (null) —DISRUPTS→ SCNN1A (HGNC:10604); SCNN1A (HGNC:10604) —BINDS→ Epithelial Sodium Channel (ENaC) activity (GO:0005349); Epithelial Sodium Channel (ENaC) activity (GO:0005349) —DECREASES→ Sodium reabsorption (null); Sodium reabsorption (null) —LEADS_TO→ Pseudohypoaldosteronism, type IB1 (MONDO:0009917); Sodium reabsorption (null) —LEADS_TO→ Best disease (MONDO:0013175). Pathogenic variants in SCNN1A lead to reduced ENaC activity, impairing sodium reabsorption. This downstream effect on sodium balance contributes to the distinct phenotypes of both pseudohypoaldosteronism type IB1 and Best disease, suggesting a shared functional consequence at the level of epithelial sodium transport.

**How to falsify it:** Identification of a pathogenic variant in SCNN1A that demonstrably causes a gain-of-function effect in both disease contexts, or a complete lack of functional overlap in the downstream consequences of SCNN1A mutations on epithelial sodium transport between the two conditions. _(variant: Any common variants (AF > 0.01) in SCNN1A found at high frequency in gnomAD that do not segregate with either disease.)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of SCNN1A in these distinct diseases could reveal novel therapeutic targets for modulating ENaC activity, potentially benefiting patients with either condition. For example, therapies aimed at restoring ENaC function or compensating for its loss might be applicable across both pseudohypoaldosteronism and certain forms of Best disease.

#### 5. moyamoya disease 7  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.379)

#### 7. Liddle syndrome 3  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.327)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2672351)

**Proposed mechanism:** SCNN1A pathogenic variant (haploinsufficiency) (null) —DISRUPTS→ SCNN1A (HGNC:10612); SCNN1A (HGNC:10612) —DECREASES→ Epithelial Sodium Channel (ENaC) activity (null); Epithelial Sodium Channel (ENaC) activity (null) —LEADS_TO→ Hypertension (HP:0000827); Epithelial Sodium Channel (ENaC) activity (null) —LEADS_TO→ Hypokalemia (HP:0002177); Epithelial Sodium Channel (ENaC) activity (null) —LEADS_TO→ Metabolic alkalosis (HP:0011333); SCNN1A pathogenic variant (gain-of-function) (null) —DISRUPTS→ SCNN1A (HGNC:10612); SCNN1A (HGNC:10612) —INCREASES→ Epithelial Sodium Channel (ENaC) activity (null). **How to falsify it:** Identification of pathogenic variants in SCNN1A associated with MONDO:0013175 that demonstrably lead to *increased* ENaC activity, or identification of pathogenic variants in SCNN1A associated with Liddle syndrome 3 that demonstrably lead to *decreased* ENaC activity. _(variant: null)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the opposing functional consequences of SCNN1A variants on ENaC activity provides insights into ion channel regulation and offers potential therapeutic targets for hypertension and electrolyte imbalances.
